record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: How can hyperparameter optimization, neural architecture search, debugging, interpretability, and other centralized machine-learning workflow practices be adapted to federated learning when training is slower, resources are limited, hyperparameters include both server and client choices, and raw decentralized data cannot be inspected directly?

evidence.quote: Developing privacy-preserving techniques to answer such questions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning setting in which a global model is trained by a central server that coordinates a large, heterogeneous population of client devices. Each client holds a local dataset that cannot be transmitted, pooled, or directly inspected by the server, and clients participate in training only intermittently subject to limited compute, memory, energy, and bandwidth. A training run requires many rounds of communication in which the server broadcasts model parameters, selected clients perform local updates on their private data, and updates (possibly with privacy-preserving perturbations such as differential privacy or secure aggregation) are returned and combined. The set of tunable hyperparameters is partitioned into server-side choices (e.g., aggregation rule, server learning rate, client-sampling distribution, number of local steps per round, total round count) and client-side choices (e.g., local optimizer, local learning rate, local batch size, regularization), and individual training runs are substantially slower and more expensive than in centralized training.

Design rigorous methodologies, with provable or empirically validated guarantees, that adapt the following standard centralized machine-learning workflow practices to this setting while never directly accessing raw client data:

(a) Hyperparameter optimization: a procedure that selects server-side and client-side hyperparameters using only aggregated, privacy-preserving signals computed across clients, with sample-complexity (in number of federated rounds) and privacy cost bounds.

(b) Neural architecture search: a procedure that searches over model architectures under the same federated and privacy constraints, accounting for client resource heterogeneity.

(c) Debugging: techniques to diagnose training failures (e.g., divergence, poor convergence, data or label issues, client drift) without inspecting individual examples on devices.

(d) Interpretability: methods that produce model and prediction explanations consistent with what one would obtain from centralized data inspection, using only privacy-preserving aggregate queries.

(e) Data and model validation more generally: counterparts of exploratory data analysis, error analysis, fairness auditing, and outlier detection that operate only through aggregate, privacy-preserving queries over decentralized data.

Provide formal definitions, algorithms, and guarantees (statistical, computational, communication, and privacy) for each of (a)–(e), or prove impossibility results that delineate which centralized practices admit faithful federated analogues under the stated constraints.
artifact.status_search_result: The questions of adapting hyperparameter optimization, neural architecture search, debugging, and interpretability to federated learning are widely regarded as open research directions. While partial progress exists (e.g., FedEx and weight-sharing federated NAS, differentially private HPO, federated SHAP-style explanations), no comprehensive solution with provable guarantees across all listed workflow components has been established as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys open problems including workflow adaptation (HPO, NAS, debugging, interpretability) under federated constraints.
status_evidence.claim: The listed workflow-adaptation questions are posed as open problems in federated learning.

status_evidence.title: Federated Hyperparameter Tuning: Challenges, Baselines, and Connections to Weight-Sharing
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces FedEx and identifies federated HPO as an underexplored problem with only partial baselines.
status_evidence.claim: Federated hyperparameter optimization remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Federated Neural Architecture Search: a survey
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews federated NAS methods and notes open challenges in resource-aware, privacy-preserving search.
status_evidence.claim: Federated NAS is an active area with significant unresolved issues.
